title: Fundamentals of Counseling Theories
tagline: The maps every counselor carries into the therapy room.
welcome: You are about to meet the great systems of thought that have shaped a century of helping, and to discover which of them will live in your hands when a distressed child sits across from you.
vignette: A nine-year-old boy refuses to speak in his third session. His drawings have grown darker. His teacher reports outbursts no one can explain. Your supervisor asks a single question: which theory is guiding your next move, and why?
vignette_attr: An intake moment, drawn from supervised practice
description: This course surveys the major systems of psychotherapy with one focus held constant throughout: the child and the adolescent. We will study psychoanalytic and psychodynamic thought, Adlerian and humanistic approaches, person-centered, Gestalt, and existential work, the cognitive and behavioral family, and contemporary integrative and faith-sensitive models. For each system you will learn its view of human nature, its theory of change, its techniques, and its limits with young clients.
cases: the nine-year-old who stopped speaking, whose drawings we will learn to read
a fourteen-year-old whose anger protects a grief she cannot name
a family whose love is real but whose patterns wound, and who must learn new ones
misconceptions: that theory is academic decoration, when in fact every intervention you will ever choose is a theory in action
that one favorite approach can serve every child, when the evidence and the ethics both demand a wider repertoire
questions: What must we believe about a child before we can truly help that child?
How does a theory of change become a session plan on a difficult afternoon?
Can a counselor hold several theories and still practice with integrity?
figures: whose depth psychology taught clinicians to listen beneath the spoken word
who demonstrated that a disciplined, empathic relationship is itself an engine of change
whose cognitive model gave counseling a testable architecture for understanding distress
settings: private practice rooms designed for young clients
faith: As a biblical university, we hold that every theory must be examined with the same seriousness we bring to Scripture: tested, discerned, and put to loving use. Counseling a child is a profoundly moral act, and this course will ask you to integrate competence with conviction, so that your skill serves a vocation rather than a career.
importance: Theory is the counselor's map; without it, empathy wanders and technique drifts into guesswork
Every clinical decision you will ever justify, from play to confrontation, rests on theoretical ground
Accrediting bodies and employers expect master's-level counselors to reason theoretically, not merely technically
outcomes: Explain the major schools of counseling theory
You will describe the founding figures, core concepts, and historical movement of each system with academic precision.
Compare key concepts across theoretical systems
You will set theories side by side, view of human nature against view of human nature, and defend the comparison.
Analyze each theory's fit with young clients
You will evaluate strengths, cultural limits, and developmental cautions of every approach with children and adolescents.
You will draft your own working model of practice, coherent and defensible, ready to mature across the degree.
Apply theory to real case vignettes
You will take an unseen case and produce goals, methods, and a rationale drawn from a named theoretical position.
Reason with professional and ethical humility
You will know where each theory ends and where referral, consultation, or supervision must begin.
modules: Foundations and History of Counseling Theory
Why theories exist and what they do for clinicians
The moral and pastoral roots of modern helping
How to read a theory: assumptions, change mechanisms, evidence
Before we meet the individual systems, we must learn what a theory actually is, so you never mistake a slogan for a framework.
Psychoanalytic and Psychodynamic Approaches
Freud's structural model and its modern revisions
Defense mechanisms observable in child sessions
Object relations, attachment, and the play of transference
Depth psychology taught generations of clinicians to listen beneath the words; with children, its legacy lives in play and symbol.
Adlerian and Humanistic Approaches
Inferiority, striving, and the child's private logic
Birth order, family constellation, and lifestyle assessment
Maslow, Rogers, and the actualizing tendency in young people
Adlerian thought remains one of the most practical lenses for schools and families, and humanism guards the dignity of every young client.
Person-Centered, Gestalt, and Existential Work
The six conditions of therapeutic personality change
Contact, awareness, and unfinished business in adolescents
Meaning, freedom, and anxiety developmentally understood
These traditions teach presence itself as technique, the hardest skill in the room and the one young clients detect most quickly.
Cognitive and Behavior Therapies
Classical and operant foundations of behavior change
Cognitive distortions in child and adolescent form
The third wave: mindfulness, acceptance, and schema-aware work
The evidence base for youth anxiety, depression, and conduct difficulties leans heavily here, so your literacy must be deep and critical.
Contemporary, Integrative, and Faith-Sensitive Models
Common factors research and what actually heals
Principled eclecticism versus theoretical integration
Counseling that honors the spiritual life of the client
This is where the field is moving, and where a distinctly Christian university must think carefully, charitably, and rigorously.
Building Your Personal Theory of Practice
Mapping your assumptions about human nature and change
Drafting an integrative model with safeguards
Presenting and defending your framework to peers
The course culminates in your own written framework, the document that will quietly guide every practicum that follows.
practicum: Practice lives in three structures woven through the eighteen hours of lecture.
Theory-to-practice case seminars dissecting recorded demonstrations
Vignette laboratories: unseen cases answered from a named theory
Reflective journals tracking your evolving theoretical identity
A supervised mock-intake integrating theory choice with ethics
assessment: Assessment mirrors professional life: formulation, defense, and examination.
A theory comparison matrix across all major systems
A recorded integrative case formulation with written rationale
Seminar participation and reflective journal portfolio
A comprehensive examination covering every theoretical family
tips: Study theories in pairs, comparing as you go; contrast is how memory works
After every module, write one paragraph on how that theory would treat the boy who would not speak
Build your personal framework document early and revise it every week
integration: This course is the trunk of the tree. Child and adolescent development will give you the clients these theories must serve; ethics will govern how you use them; techniques and skills will put them into your hands. Nothing in your remaining semesters stands independent of this foundation.
closing: May these maps serve you well, and may you always remember that behind every theory stands a real child waiting to be understood.
